text:
maya: Morning async — quick checkin on kernel/batching/KV perf.

what I did: rolled a small patch to the slot allocator to avoid slot-shedding under burst-coalesce. landed in staging.
blocked: seeing a weird p95 spike when microbatch size toggles between 4/8.
plan today: run controlled bench runs across A100 pools and validate fallback path.

oliver: nice. can you paste the bench run config? wondering if the jitter is from warm-lane priming.

maya: sure, pasted below:

```yaml
bench_id: priming-2026-03-20-01
model: redwood-cpu-7b-quant
microbatch_size: [4,8]
sequence_len: 512
concurrent_requests: 48
kv_cache_limit_gb: 18
warmup_prefixes: 200
repeat: 5
```

jen: re: kv_cache_limit — did you try the slot-less eviction patch? that reduced tail for me on small shards.

maya: i did a canary. eviction decreases cold-hit p95 but increases p50 for small seq lengths. tradeoff unclear.

sam: quick ping — PR #432 is ready for review, contains the slot allocator fix and updated metrics. maya, you added the microbatch toggle, can you add a short note in the PR about the p95 regression? makes triage easier.

maya: will do, adding benchmarks + traces. also attaching one trace snippet below.

```text
trace: slot-alloc-2026-03-20-01
path: /srv/traces/priming/slot-alloc-1.json
span: allocate_slot -> wait_for_kv (delay 23ms)
span: batch_coalesce -> kernel_dispatch (delay 12ms)
note: repeated backpressure during microbatch switch
```

deploy-bot: CI passed for branch/slot-alloc-fix (build 9876) :white_check_mark:

jen: thanks — i'll review PR after standup. if the p95 holds on your full run, should we try smaller kv_cache_limit (16GB) to see if it's cache thrash?

oliver: also, we should test with slot-shedding disabled to isolate allocator behavior. maya, can you run a 30min run with shed=false and post metrics?

maya: yep running now, 30min start 1749876600; will post results here.

sam: FYI scheduling a microbench slot at 11:30 PT to reproduce on D-vpool.

maya: results: short summary — with shed=false p95 improved by ~18%, but token throughput dropped ~6%. attaching numbers:

- shed=true: p50 34ms, p95 240ms, tps 3200
- shed=false: p50 40ms, p95 197ms, tps 3010

conclusion: slot-shedding favours throughput, hurts tail. propose a tunable threshold for heavy-tail workloads.

jen: sounds reasonable. we can surface that tunable in the runtime config and add an experiment in Optimize.

oliver: agree. want me to draft a small dashboard to track shed events vs p95? could help rollout.

maya: please yes. i've opened issue #1092 with findings and marked as p1 for perf team.

sam: thanks team. quick blockers? anyone needing help with traces/bench infra?

jen: none from me.

oliver: i'll take dashboard and a quickset of queries.

maya: i'm good for now. will ping if the longer run shows new anomalies. :coffee:
